title: Feature Learning Dynamics in Infinite-Depth ResNets
claim: Approximation error to the limiting dynamics shrinks at a consistent power-law rate in both depth and width, so the two limits commute.
layout: 4 panels in a row, log-log error curves, dashed reference line
description: A single horizontal strip of four log-log line plots. Every panel plots MSE on the y-axis. Panels 1 and 3 use depth on the x-axis, with one curve per network width (32 to 1024). Panels 2 and 4 use width on the x-axis, with one curve per depth (4 to 128). The curves are colored on a sequential light-orange to dark-purple palette, and each panel has a legend in its lower left. A dashed gray line marked 1/L or 1/n is the theoretical-rate reference. In every panel the colored curves fall roughly parallel to the dashed line, which shows the predicted decay. The first two panels show the network at initialization and the last two show it after 30 training epochs. The eye goes first to the steep downward-sloping curves and the dashed diagonal.
caption: Convergence to NFD at initialization and after training. Depth-$\mu$P ResNets are evaluated on CIFAR-10 with SGD. The first two panels show convergence with depth and width at initialization, and the last two after 30 training epochs. Across settings, the error decays consistently with $\mathcal{O}(1/L+1/n)$, supporting the commutativity of the width and depth limits.
abstract: Deep neural networks have achieved remarkable success in practice, yet a mechanistic understanding of how features evolve during training remains incomplete, particularly in the large-depth limit. We investigate this question in residual networks (ResNets) with single-layer blocks trained by SGD under depth-$\mu$P. Tracking these dynamics is challenging because backpropagation couples forward features and backward gradients via the reuse of weight matrices $W_\ell$ and their transposes $W_\ell^\top$. To isolate this structural dependence, we derive exact conditional Gaussian representations that isolate the weight-reuse effect at finite width and depth. At initialization, its effect vanishes at rate $O(n^{-1/2})$ in coordinatewise $L^p$ uniformly in depth. This allows the joint forward and backward processes to converge to their continuous-depth limits at coordinatewise $L^p$ rates of $O(n^{-1/2}+L^{-1})$ and $O(n^{-1/2}+L^{-1/2})$, respectively, for every $p\geq 2$. After one SGD update, features evolve according to a stochastic differential equation whose drift incorporates both the direct SGD contribution and a persistent response to the initial backward pass. We bound the $L^p$ approximation error for the updated features and network output by $C_{p,L}n^{-1/2} + C_pL^{-1/2}$. However, a linear ResNet counterexample demonstrates that updated feature moments can diverge as depth grows at fixed width, showing that the width and depth limits need not commute. Finally, for multiple updates, we derive mean-field recursions by tracking accumulated feature and gradient histories, recovering the $C_{p,L}n^{-1/2} + C_p L^{-1/2}$ convergence rate under nondegeneracy conditions on the history Gram matrices.
